newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day Cetes rate down to 22.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day Cetes rate down to 22.50 pct.

text.p: Mexico's same-day Cetes rates closed down 100 basis points to 22.50 percent on Monday, the lowest level since December 1994.
Dealers said the decline was due to good liquidity in the system, expectations of lower primary rates at the upcoming Banco de Mexico Cetes auction and low volume during the trading session.

"They (Banco de Mexico) want to keep primary rates going down. Short-term paper was the only thing being traded and there was money in the market. The few trade were able to move the rates," said one dealer.
Bank notes and acceptances, including pagares, closed down 15 basis points to 24.60 percent.
However, pressure on the peso and an increase in the rate on the U.S. 30-year bond slowed declines in the Mexican rates.
"Markets were nervous, but there is nothing to fear with the changes to the exchange rate because this follows with Banco de Mexico policies," said one dealer.
The spot 48-hour peso contract closed down 1.35 centavos to 7.5050/7.5090 per dollar.
Due to a government expense payment the central bank only injected 3.412 billion pesos into the secondary market.
Dealers expect a quiet session on Tuesday with levels near 23.0 percent for the Cetes and a shortfall of about 4.0 billion pesos.
